text.p: The creator of the smash Irish show "Riverdance" won a Grammy Award, the U.S. music industry's top honour, for best musical show album on Wednesday.

Bill Whelan, a prolific Irish composer, songwriter and record producer, first conceived "Riverdance" in 1994 as an act to be performed during the Eurovision Song Contest, a hugely popular annual pop song competition.
"Riverdance" was later expanded into a full-length song and dance extravaganza featuring the explosive blows of the dancers' traditional Irish clogs and tautly synchronized choreography.

The album "Riverdance" enjoyed massive global success. In addition to going double platinum in Ireland, the album has had staggering sales in England and Australia and reached the top of U.S. magazine Billboard's world music chart.
Whelan, who has worked with Irish musical stars such as Van Morrison and U2, dedicated his Grammy to the "Riverdance" dancer-performers who have wooed audiences around the world.
The troupe also performed during the award gala, televised around the world.
"Riverdance" sold out its engagement last year in New York, where it is scheduled to return later this year.
